rules.title: Tenants Rights and Resources Ordinance
rules.requirement: Owners, landlords and management companies must give tenants and lawful occupants a Tenants Rights and Resources Guide at the start of a tenancy and again when legal steps to terminate the tenancy are taken, such as a Notice to Quit or Summary Process. The ordinance does not bar evictions otherwise allowed by law.
rules.key_value: Guide must be provided at tenancy inception and termination
rules.penalty: Fine of $300 for each day's violation
rules.citation: Chapter 8.71 of the Cambridge Municipal Code

exempt_if.name: health_or_treatment_facility
exempt_if.text: rental units in a hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility or in a non-profit facility that has the primary purpose of providing short term assistance, treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug or other substance abuse

exempt_if.name: short_term_rental
exempt_if.text: Short Term Rental Units as set forth in Article 4, Section 4.60 of the Cambridge Zoning Ordinance

coverage.summary: Applies to residential rental agreements, including a single residential dwelling unit.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Does not apply to units in hospitals, nursing or health facilities, short-term substance abuse treatment facilities, or short term rental units.

rules.quoted_span: It is required to provide this Guide at the inception and termination of tenancies. The Ordinance also requires that a landlord provide the Guide to tenants when legal steps to terminate a tenancy are taken (ex. Notice to Quit or Summary Process).

repairs.0c58f6c2a8d401f443e2b91445c962990fa52f91: It is required to provide this Guide at the inception and termination of tenancies. For new tenancies, the Guide must be provided when a tenant signs a lease or enters into a tenancy agreement for the first time or tenders the first month’s rent. The Ordinance also requires that a landlord provide the Guide to tenants when legal steps to terminate a tenancy are taken (ex. Notice to Quit or Summary Process).
